verdict.rationale: ROS 2 provides SROS2/DDS-Security, with participant authentication, encryption, and security enclaves that each hold a policy governing ROS communications. This lets an operator restrict which nodes can take part in the graph, and by extension which can publish commands, set parameters, or subscribe to data. However, it is node- and participant-level communication security, not a human-facing role and permission system per robot, and it requires manual keystore and policy work. Missing for 10: user/operator role definitions, explicit per-robot command/configure/view permission tiers, a management UI or tooling for assigning roles, detailed documentation of the permission-policy model, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
